title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Group All 1s Together
statement: Given a binary array `nums`, return the minimum number of adjacent swaps required to group all 1's together in any contiguous subarray. The array is circular, meaning the first and last elements are adjacent.
summary: Find the minimum adjacent swaps needed to group all 1s in a circular binary array.

examples.explanation: There are 3 ones. We can group them by swapping the 0 at index 2 with the 1 at index 3 (one swap) to get [0,1,1,1,0,0,0].
There are 5 ones. Best window of 5 consecutive elements (considering circularity) has 3 ones already, so we need 2 swaps to bring the remaining 2 ones into the window.

The array is already grouped in circular sense: the two 1s at ends and one in middle? Actually [1,1,0,0,1] -> in circular view, the 1s at index 0,1 and 4 are adjacent via circularity, so they form a group of three? Wait, no: only if we consider wrapping. The ones are at 0,1,4. In circular array, 4 and 0 are adjacent, so we have a block [4,0,1] which is three consecutive in circular sense. So yes, already grouped.
